storm.summary_layperson: No storms anywhere nearby tonight — clear, dry, cool northerly air with nothing on radar and no weather alerts.
storm.local_effect_blurb: The Sound's cooling buffer is already fading — the air–water gap is about 6°F now and drops below the ~5°F threshold around 4:15 PM, reversing to the air being colder than the water (about −7°F) by 8 PM — but with no storms around it doesn't matter tonight.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: A dry, settled northerly flow covers the whole region. The Upton (KOKX) radar shows no echoes to track, there are no NWS watches, warnings or advisories, and the atmosphere has no storm fuel at all — convective energy (CAPE) is 0 J/kg and wind shear is a light 8 kt. Dewpoints in the upper 30s confirm very dry air.

Local modifier: On warm days, Long Island Sound acts as a buffer — cool water under warmer air forms a stable “marine layer” that tends to weaken storms crossing it. Right now the water is 62°F and the air is about 68°F, a modest 6°F gap. But the Sound holds its temperature while the air cools after sunset (6:05 PM tonight), so that gap closes fast: it falls below the ~5°F threshold around 4:15 PM, is near 3°F by 5 PM, and by 8 PM the air (about 55°F) is actually colder than the water. There is no sea breeze running today either — the wind is blowing off the land.

Most likely outcome: A quiet, storm-free evening for the cove and every surrounding town alike. With nothing to deflect, the local effects are simply not in play — the cove is no better or worse off than inland Westchester or Fairfield County tonight.

What would change the call: Only something unforecast — a new echo appearing on radar to the west or an NWS alert. Neither the model nor the forecast offices show any sign of that through the evening.

wind.regime_label: Moderate northerly gradient wind — no sea breeze
wind.tactics_blurb: Northerly breeze blowing off the land, so it's puffy and shifty with big swings between gusts and lulls, and it holds through sunset at around 7–8 kt. Stay in the middle of the cove away from the shoreline wind shadows, and tack on the big headers.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
The call: Moderate gradient wind — no sea breeze in play (B-moderate). The well-sited airport anemometers around the Sound average 11.6 kt from the north to north-northeast, and the air–water temperature difference is only 5.6°F, right at the edge of what a sea breeze needs. More decisively, not one of 24 coastal or inland stations shows any southerly component, so no sea breeze has formed. Because this is a gradient-wind day, not a sea-breeze day, the sea-breeze direction correction does not apply and there is no sunset collapse to worry about.

Right now at RYC: NNE 4 kt instantaneous, 10-minute average 8.1 kt, gusting 15 — a big gust-to-lull spread typical of wind coming off the land. The model (HRRR) is running about 2 kt lighter than RYC is actually reading, so the hourly numbers above are nudged up to match the cove.

Where the pressure is: In a north-to-north-northeast wind the breeze reaches the cove after crossing Greenwich's trees and houses, so it arrives in puffs with holes between them. The steadiest average pressure is usually mid-cove, away from the lee of either shore. Expect the strongest puffs to roll down off the northern and northwestern shore.

Shift character: Oscillating, not persistent — offshore flow typically swings 15–30° between puffs. The model shows a slow drift to the left (from about 10° toward 350°) through the evening, so lean slightly toward the left-hand shifts late, but mostly play the oscillations: tack on the big headers and stay connected to the puffs. Stations disagree on direction (agreement only 0.5 across the area, with inland stations reading west-northwest), which is another sign of a shifty, terrain-chopped breeze rather than a front.

Through the window: Unlike a sea breeze, this wind doesn't care about the sun — it holds through the 6:05 PM sunset. After dark the lower atmosphere stabilizes, so the gusts should soften (from mid-teens toward ~10 kt) while the average stays around 7–8 kt. That's the sweet spot for one-design dinghies — good racing, but stay alert for the lulls. It will be chilly: air dropping from the upper 60s into the mid-50s by 8 PM.

data_caveats: HRRR model data only available through 8 PM (forecast hours 6–12 failed to download) — 9–10 PM wind is extrapolated from the evening trend and is lower confidence.
